svg.title: Where axolotls live
svg.desc: A simplified diagram of the south of Mexico City. Axolotls survive only in the canals of Lake Xochimilco, a grid of waterways between floating gardens called chinampas, with the city built right up to the edge. Estimates of the wild population range from 50 to 1,000, and a recent survey of 115 sites found none by sight, detecting them only through DNA in the water. Eighteen captive-bred axolotls released with radio tags all survived, and local farmers have built 21 filtered refuge pools.

text.font-family: Georgia, serif

text.font-family: -apple-system, Segoe UI, Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: A handful of canals in the south of Mexico City. That is the entire wild world.
